Some of the Israelites, having neglected the fear of God and despised the hunting of the Lord, but the prophet Ezekiel says the Lord's word came to him, saying, 'Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel, and say to those prophesying from their heart, and prophesying, and say to them: Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: Because your words are false and your divinations are empty, therefore I am against you, says the Lord. I will stretch out my hand against the prophets who see false visions and who speak empty words.' Since women also were weaving a wicked spell of knowledge of things to come, God said again to the prophet, 'And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy from their heart, and prophesy against them, and say: Thus says the Lord: Woe to those who sew cushions on every elbow and make veils for every head of every age, to turn souls away. Souls of my people were turned away, and they were making souls perish and were profaning me before my people for a handful of barley and a piece of bread, to kill souls that should not die, and to keep alive souls that should not live; when you speak to the people who listen to empty words.' For the truth is that those who prophesy do not transport people to other laws by the law of our prophecy beyond the mind.

Having composed speeches similar to those they are accustomed to, they send out from the workshops of deceit. They claim to be skilled and wise, and to have advanced in their craft and precision, and having pretended to understand the affairs of others accurately and without error, they are so deceived about their own affairs that they would say they have not experienced the consequences of their actions. Although it is easy for the one who knows beforehand to guard against and escape the predicted outcome, why do they not run ahead of the dangers of others, although they have trusted in their craft? Therefore, their discoveries are rightly considered deceitful, and through them, the truth of our affairs is revealed. But, they say, some of what was said has turned out to be true. And indeed, this is what the scripture says, and what you should be mindful of. Then, one who is fleeing and being pursued, will he make an apology for his crimes? For we do not consider it true that some of what was said has turned out to be true, and we are not putting our trust in what is not shameful. The fact that he does not see everything as true would be a clear proof of the disgust that is in you, and it would show that their pursuit is still sinful, and their craft is full of nonsense, and their lesson is laughable, although they would not deny the things that God knows. For the divine and incorruptible mind knows all things that will happen, and if it were to speak to some, whether they speak to others, it is not a false narrative.

The discoveries of human conceptions are more a product of conjecture than a pursuit of truth, and each person's opinions seem to be influenced by their passions and bodily concerns, rather than a genuine search for wisdom, and they think they can hit the mark, but in reality, they are often off target, and their boasts are empty, and they are ridiculed by others, but the one who is healthy in their understanding does not boast about one thing, and they are not puffed up, but rather they are mindful of their limitations, and they are ashamed to boast about the mistakes of others, and they do not pretend to have knowledge they do not have, and they do not ask for praise from others, but rather they acknowledge their ignorance, and they are humble in their pursuit of wisdom

Holy prophets have been among us, not accustomed to measuring the movement of stars, nor meddling with the needs of elements, and not being forced into things that are not fitting for human nature, nor having been emboldened by vain deceptions; but rather, from a divine revelation of the Spirit, foreseeing future things and having proclaimed to us from afar the times; nothing of what was said has been disproven; rather, the nature of things creeps forward in time, more precisely according to the things that have already been proclaimed; for God was the one speaking; therefore, it is clear that those prophets rejected the deadly and mercenary astrological deception; for they said, thus says the Lord, do not learn from the ways of the nations, and do not fear the signs of the sky, for the thoughts of the nations are vain; the stars that adorn the sky with their multitude and beauty have been for the use and times of those who made them; but they are subject to the laws of the one who made them, and they signal the changes of the seasons to those on earth, sometimes rising and sometimes setting; therefore, one should pay attention, not to those things…
pass_b_english: The idea of having a notion is presented, and it is said that the rebuke is just according to those who are esteemed in the highest dignity.

The one who is esteemed in the highest dignity, having been arrayed in my armor, says to the soldier, 'You think the things of barbarians; but I, because you only wish to be seen, being entirely of others.'
It seems that God also speaks about those who are not established in faith, saying that this people honors Him with their lips, but their heart is far from Him (Isaiah 29:13).
They worship Him in vain, keeping the teachings and commandments of men, which are nothing but human traditions.
Time changes the expression to what is beneficial, and some people have rushed into abomination, paying attention to spirits of error and giving their mind to false and deceitful prophecies.
They pay attention to the movement of the stars and pull the healthy and unerring glory, and those who are easy to carry away and prone to deception.
They do not see the things above, but imagine they know the things under the earth, and they deceive themselves, being cowardly, and destroy others with their own heads.
They persuade people to be initiated into their false beliefs, promising knowledge of future things and special divine superiority.
They use deceitful speeches, and the things that are beneath, they hint at with some foolish and deceitful speeches, and the barely collected money is stolen.
For the art of cold and unlawful gains is their guardian, and the writing on the public tablet, they make a false and deceitful marketplace.
Some of the Israelites had become complacent in their fear of God and had begun to despise the Lord's prophetic work.
The prophet Ezekiel received a word from the Lord, which said, 'Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are prophesying from their own hearts' (Ezekiel 13:2).

The Lord's message was clear: because their words were false and their divinations empty, He would be against them, and He declared that He would stretch out His hand against the prophets who saw false visions and spoke empty words.
Furthermore, the Lord spoke against the women who were weaving a wicked spell of knowledge, turning people's souls away from the truth.
He said, 'Woe to those who sew cushions on every elbow and make veils for every head of every age, to turn souls away' (Ezekiel 13:18).

These women were making souls perish and profaning the Lord's name before His people, all for a handful of barley and a piece of bread, to kill souls that should not die, and to keep alive souls that should not live; when you speak to the people who listen to empty words.
For the truth is that true prophecy does not lead people to follow other laws or empty words, but rather to follow the law of the Lord.
Those who compose speeches that resemble the ones they are accustomed to send out deceitful messages from their workshops of deceit.

They claim to be skilled and wise, having advanced in their craft and precision, but they are deceived about their own affairs and would say they have not experienced the consequences of their actions.
Although it is easy for someone who knows beforehand to guard against and escape the predicted outcome, why do they not run ahead of the dangers of others, despite trusting in their craft?
Their discoveries are rightly considered deceitful, and through them, the truth of our affairs is revealed.
But they say that some of what was said has turned out to be true, and indeed, this is what the scripture says, and what we should be mindful of.
One who is fleeing and being pursued will not make an apology for their crimes, for we do not consider it true that some of what was said has turned out to be true.

The fact that they do not see everything as true would be a clear proof of the disgust that is in them, and it would show that their pursuit is still sinful, and their craft is full of nonsense, and their lesson is laughable.
Human conceptions are often the product of conjecture rather than a genuine pursuit of truth.
Each person's opinions seem to be influenced by their passions and bodily concerns, and they think they can hit the mark, but their boasts are empty, and they are ridiculed by others.

The one who is healthy in their understanding does not boast about one thing, and they are not puffed up, and they do not pretend to have knowledge they do not have, and they do not ask for praise from others.
The holy prophets who were among us did not concern themselves with measuring the movement of the stars or meddling with the needs of elements.
Rather, they received a divine revelation of the Spirit, which enabled them to foresee future events and proclaim them to us from afar.
As a result, their words have proven to be true, and the nature of things has unfolded in time, precisely as they had foretold, for it was God who spoke through them.
The prophets rejected the deadly and mercenary astrological deception, which is based on the ways of the nations.
As the Lord says, we should not learn from the ways of the nations, nor should we fear the signs of the sky, for the thoughts of the nations are vain (Jeremiah 10:2).
